name: Rise of Empires
description: November 1444: the day after Varna, where King Władysław of Poland and Hungary fell before Murad II's army, Byzantium is reduced to Constantinople and the Morea, England and France sit out a truce in the Hundred Years' War, Burgundy rules the Low Countries and Ming China, the Timurids and Vijayanagara dominate Asia.
approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, which at this resolution merge many states of 1444: the province of each modern cluster goes to whoever held most of it, so Calais, Ceuta, Ragusa, Siena, Lucca, Mantua, Ferrara, Montferrat, Navarre, Holstein, the Hanseatic cities and most of the Holy Roman Empire's hundreds of lordships, bishoprics and free cities are not shown separately. The Empire's principal states stand for their regions (Bavaria includes Franconia, Württemberg includes Baden and Swabia, the Palatinate includes the electorates of Mainz and Trier, Cologne includes Westphalia, Jülich and Cleves, Saxony includes Thuringia and Magdeburg, Pomerania includes Mecklenburg, Burgundy includes Utrecht and Guelders, which became Burgundian clients only in 1456 and 1473). Some cities fall in a neighbour's province: Constantinople's province includes Kocaeli, so Byzantium looks larger than it was; Genoa's own coast lies in Florence's Tuscan province, so Genoa is shown with Corsica and Chios-Lesbos; Granada is drawn as the Córdoba-Jaén-Granada province, so it appears larger than the Nasrid emirate; Venice's Bergamo and Brescia are Milanese; Franche-Comté is Lorraine's and Bresse Savoy's. Poland and Lithuania, which had separate rulers in November 1444 (Casimir became king of Poland only in 1447), are separate allied countries; Masovia is a Polish subject, Moldavia a Polish subject, Wallachia a Hungarian subject, Cyprus, Dulkadir and the Sharifate of Mecca Mamluk subjects. Serbia and Byzantium paid tribute to the Ottomans but are shown independent so that they do not join the Ottoman war; Candar (Kastamonu) is folded into the Ottoman Empire, Vyatka into Muscovy, Jaffna into Kotte, Navarre into Aragon. The Varna crusade is modelled as a running Hungarian-Ottoman war; the Castilian noble wars, the Old Zürich War, the Soest Feud, the Muscovite civil war and the Saxon Fratricidal War are internal and are shown only as low stability. The Truce of Tours is a non-aggression pact between England and France. Population (millions), GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars, Maddison-style) and army sizes are rounded estimates with wide uncertainty, very wide outside Europe and China. Mamluk Egypt is a military government and the Ashikaga shogunate a military regime; Tibet's regime is shown as a theocracy; steppe khanates, the Gaelic lordships, the Hausa and Mossi kingdoms and the Mixtec-Zapotec states are single decentralised polities. Technology follows the game's Eurasian tree: American societies lag by thousands of years (no iron, horses or wheels), sub-Saharan Africa by centuries. Lands without states of the period are left unowned: most of the Americas and Africa, Siberia, the Wild Fields of Ukraine, Circassia, the Sahara, Arabia's interior, the Turkmen and Baloch tribal lands, Manchuria's Jurchens, Lapland and Greenland (the Norse settlements were gone by c. 1450), Hokkaido, the Philippines and most of the Indonesian islands; Orkney and Shetland, Norwegian until 1468-69, fall in a Scottish province. Flags are simplified standards.
